title: Jeremiah's seventy years (Jer 25:11–12; 29:10; read in Dan 9:2)
speaker: Jeremiah
description: The nations will serve the king of Babylon seventy years; when they are completed Babylon will be punished (Jer 25:11–12) and the exiles visited and returned (29:10). Daniel reads it as seventy years "for the desolations of Jerusalem" (Dan 9:2).
in_text_interpretation: Later biblical texts apply it differently: 2 Chr 36:21–22 to the land's sabbath rest until the kingdom of Persia and Cyrus's first year; Zech 1:12 (Darius's second year) to "these seventy years" of indignation against Jerusalem; Dan 9:24 extends it to seventy weeks.

interpretations.label: Babylonian supremacy: c. 609/605 to 539/538 BC
proponents: S. R. Driver (1900): "the 70 years of the Chaldaean supremacy"
D. Guzik (counting from 605, the first deportation)
interpretations.summary: Textual reasoning: Jer 25:11 speaks of the nations serving the king of Babylon; 25:12 ends the period with Babylon's punishment. Historical evidence: Babylon fell in Oct 539 (Nabonidus Chronicle) and Cyrus's first Babylonian year began Nisan 538. Objection: 605–539 is 66 years, so "seventy" is taken as round or the end point moved later (Guzik: the period still had "three or four years" to run at Dan 9).

referents.referent: From Babylon's rise over Judah to its fall

interpretations.label: Desolation of the Temple: 587/586 to 516/515 BC
proponents: Zechariah 1:12; 7:5 (text, in Darius I's 2nd and 4th years)
Jerome ("seventy years for the desolation of the Temple")
interpretations.summary: Textual reasoning: in Darius I's second year (Zech 1:7, 12) the angel still speaks of "these seventy years" of indignation against Jerusalem, and the Temple was finished in Darius's sixth year (Ezra 6:15). From the destruction (587/586) to the completion (Adar 515) is about 70 years (operator arithmetic). Objection: Jeremiah's own wording is about serving Babylon, not the Temple.

referents.referent: From the Temple's destruction to its rebuilding

interpretations.label: The land's sabbaths, ended by Cyrus's decree (Chronicler)
interpretations.summary: The Chronicler joins Jeremiah's seventy years to the land enjoying its sabbaths (Lev 26:34–35) "until the reign of the kingdom of Persia", and dates Cyrus's proclamation to his first year "that the LORD's word by Jeremiah's mouth might be accomplished". Driver notes that Dan 9:24 develops this sabbatical reading into seventy weeks of years. Guzik: about 490 years of neglected sabbath years left the land owing seventy, collected in the exile; he gives no start or end year.

referents.referent: The land's sabbath rest until Cyrus
